title: release-and-rollback refuses a one-way migration on a rolling deploy
prompt: Act as the sre agent. Plan this afternoon's deploy of migration 003 and the matching change to src/user-service.js. CONTEXT.md has the production details.
expectations: The agent answers the rollback question before planning the rollout.
It identifies that dropping first_name and last_name is irreversible: the original values cannot be recovered from full_name, so rollback loses data.
It identifies the rolling-deploy incompatibility: old instances still write first_name and last_name while new instances read full_name, and both serve traffic for about ten minutes.
It proposes the expand-and-contract sequence across separate deploys — add the column, backfill, write both, read new, and drop the old columns only in a later release once usage is measured at zero.
It flags the backfill UPDATE over roughly 30 million rows as a locking and duration risk, and proposes batching.
The plan states an abort criterion as a number from a named query, not as a judgement call.
The plan names the three observability questions: is the new path taken, is it succeeding, how long does it take.
must_not: A plan was produced that ships migration 003 as written this afternoon.
Rollback is described as 'roll forward if there is a problem'.
The rolling-deploy window is not mentioned at all.
grade: The migration is written to look routine. Producing a tidy rollout plan for it, without noticing that it cannot be undone, is the failure being tested.
